stories.title: Accenture faces tougher regulatory environment
stories.summary: Accenture ranked tenth on a CIBC list of stocks to buy following the Democratic election sweep. The bank designed the basket to withstand a less business friendly environment, citing a potentially tougher regulatory backdrop for corporate America. The firm is now navigating a shift in market sentiment.

stories.title: Qantas partners with Accenture for system overhaul
stories.summary: Qantas has signed a partnership with Accenture to modernise back end systems and data. The airline aims to replace over 1,000 legacy applications that were never designed to work together. The project coincides with the largest fleet renewal in the company history.

stories.title: Deloitte recruits KPMG restructuring team
stories.summary: Deloitte has hired KPMG Australia national restructuring leader Tim Mableson along with partners James Dampney and Peter Gothard. The move transfers a group of insolvency specialists to a major competitor. The team previously worked at Ferrier Hodgson before its 2019 acquisition by KPMG.

stories.title: KPMG Pakistan leaves global network
stories.summary: KPMG Pakistan has separated from the global network to operate independently as Taseer Hadi Khalid and Co. The move follows disagreements over plans for a more centralised regional management structure. The firm has operated for nearly four decades and says it will continue trading.

stories.title: McKinsey appoints three new partners in Africa
stories.summary: McKinsey and Company has appointed Kemi Onabanjo, Marilyn Kimeu and Tola Sunmonu-Balogun as partners. The three leaders were promoted from within the firm and are based in Lagos and Nairobi. They focus on economic development and large scale transformations across sub Saharan Africa.

stories.title: Accenture awaits unfair dismissal ruling
stories.summary: Accenture is currently awaiting a Court of Appeal ruling regarding an unfair dismissal case. Further details are available to subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Audit firms increase pay to retain staff
stories.summary: Audit and advisory firms have rolled out 10 to 15 percent pay hikes this year to retain employees ahead of mandatory audit rotations. Some top performers received increases of up to 28 percent. Compensation is increasingly being linked to how employees use artificial intelligence tools.

stories.title: Australia considers breaking up major accounting firms
stories.summary: Australia is weighing a potential break up of the Big Four accounting firms following recent scandals. Further details are available to subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Government expands in house consulting capacity
stories.summary: The government is growing its in house consulting unit while ASIC urges auditors to improve performance. A new advisory council has been established to provide guidance to the local firm leader. The sector continues to adjust to shifting internal and external demands.

stories.title: McKinsey Nordic private equity investment struggles
stories.summary: McKinsey is facing challenges with its private equity investment in the Nordic region. Further details are available to subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Minister questions professional role in state capture
stories.summary: Justice Minister Mmamoloko Kubayi has questioned the accountability of professionals involved in state capture. The minister noted that corruption requires accountants, lawyers and consultants to facilitate the movement of money. The inquiry focuses on the role of expertise in hiding wrongdoing.

stories.title: Banking sector weighs agentic AI strategy
stories.summary: Banking CEOs are evaluating how agentic AI might disrupt industry economics over the next five years. The technology could lower barriers to entry and reset costs while altering competitive moats. Banks are now determining which customer relationships are worth defending in an automated era.

stories.title: Bain says AI strategy determines banking winners
stories.summary: Bain and Company reports that AI will reshape banking competition over the next five years. The firm argues that banks must set competitive strategies before applying AI to protect profits. The technology is presented as a means to extend market leadership positions.

stories.title: India ranked as AI rising contender by BCG
stories.summary: Boston Consulting Group has ranked India among its AI Rising Contenders, citing a strong pool of talent as a primary advantage. The country shows high readiness for adoption with relatively low exposure to disruption. India remains in the second highest category of AI maturity.

stories.title: Workplace divide grows over AI benefits
stories.summary: Seven in ten senior leaders expect AI to help firms achieve new goals, while only one third of entry level employees agree. More than three in ten workers report witnessing no meaningful benefit from the technology. Investors are increasingly questioning the returns on AI spending.

stories.title: Bain links AI procurement to earnings growth
stories.summary: Companies that redesign procurement around AI are seeing returns of up to five times their investment, according to Bain and Company. The firm reports productivity gains exceeding 60 percent. Procurement is being repositioned from a cost control function to a driver of corporate earnings.

stories.title: McKinsey says AI could automate bank risk tasks
stories.summary: McKinsey reports that AI could automate 60 to 70 percent of manual operational tasks in bank risk functions. The firm suggests lenders redirect released capacity toward strategic advisory and technology development. Automation is expected to handle routine data gathering and spreadsheet cross checking.

stories.title: BCG reports revenue growth for AI leaders
stories.summary: Boston Consulting Group reports that AI leaders in the industrial sector are growing revenues twice as fast as laggards. Further details are available to subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: AI goods drive 80% of Asia export growth
stories.summary: AI-related goods generated about 80% of Asia's recent export growth, according to Capital Economics. Indonesia, Japan and India are largely missing out, as they are not shipping the hardware data centres require. Asia's ability to ride out the recent energy shock has rested on that hardware.

stories.title: McKinsey says banks could automate 70% of risk tasks
stories.summary: Artificial intelligence could eliminate 60 to 70 per cent of manual operational tasks in banks' risk functions, according to McKinsey. The report suggests lenders could redirect resources towards strategic decision-making and AI development. The remaining 30 to 40 per cent of tasks will presumably still require a human.

stories.title: Marshall & Stevens acquires Baumann Moreau
stories.summary: Los Angeles-based valuation firm Marshall & Stevens has acquired Tampa-based Baumann Moreau. Founded in 2007, the boutique consultancy provides forensic accounting and expert witness services for litigation. The acquisition is intended to strengthen the firm's presence in the Florida market and expand its litigation support practice.

stories.summary: Onterris makes acquisitions in Australia and Texas Onterris, formerly Montrose Environmental Group, has acquired EcOz Environmental Consulting. stories.title: Marsh to acquire investment firm Wilshire
stories.summary: Marsh has agreed to acquire Wilshire, an investment consulting firm with $221 billion in assets under management. The deal expands Marsh’s footprint into the advisor-led wealth market and adds capabilities in alternative investments and data analytics. The firm currently advises institutional investors across public and private retirement plans.

stories.title: eClerx acquires RegEdge for compliance services
stories.summary: eClerx Services has acquired RegEdge, a boutique consultancy specializing in risk and regulatory services for financial institutions. The move aims to deepen eClerx’s expertise in AI-powered analytics and automation. The company says the acquisition will help clients navigate complex regulatory requirements more effectively.

stories.title: Cambridge Management Consulting acquires Alpine Resourcing
stories.summary: Cambridge Management Consulting has acquired Alpine Resourcing to bolster its UK public sector offering. Alpine Resourcing describes itself as a provider of guidance and strategic advice based on experience. The acquisition combines Alpine’s central government services with the existing government practice at Cambridge Management Consulting.

stories.title: Marsh to acquire investment consulting firm Wilshire - Reinsurance News
stories.summary: Marsh, the professional services firm providing insurance, risk management and advisory services, has agreed to acquire Wilshire, a global investment consulting, solutions, and analytics firm that serves institutional investors and financial intermediaries. stories.title: PLI schemes reach 28% of employment target
stories.summary: India's production-linked incentive schemes have achieved 76% of their investment target but only 28% of their employment goal as of March 2026, according to NITI Aayog. The report highlights an uneven translation of the government's manufacturing push into job creation. The schemes are still in progress.

stories.title: NITI Aayog reports strong progress in PLI scheme
stories.summary: A NITI Aayog report states that nearly 70 percent of targeted segments in the government's PLI scheme are on track. As of March 2026, the initiative has attracted ₹2,40,138 crore in investments and generated production worth ₹22,66,412 crore. The scheme aims to strengthen domestic manufacturing.

stories.title: Manufacturing growth hits 10.8 percent
stories.summary: NITI Aayog Vice Chairman Ashok Lahiri described the 10.8 percent growth in India's manufacturing sector as a respectable performance. While the overall economy grows at 7 to 7.5 percent, Lahiri expressed an ambition for the sector to reach 12 percent. If it hits that target, he plans to ask for

stories.title: Retail inflation breaches RBI upper limit
stories.summary: India's retail inflation rose to 6.09 percent in October, exceeding the Reserve Bank of India's 6 percent upper tolerance limit for the first time since the new series began in January 2026. Food inflation reached 8.94 percent, driven by elevated prices and an unfavourable base effect.

stories.title: NITI Aayog seeks framework for gold mining
stories.summary: NITI Aayog CEO Anurag Jain has called for a robust evaluation framework for awarding gold exploration and mining projects. The proposal aims to address geological data gaps, lengthy project timelines, and investment viability to reduce India's dependence on imported gold. The country currently has significant untapped resources.

stories.title: Haldiram Snacks begins IPO process
stories.summary: Haldiram Snacks Food has appointed EY to manage its initial public offering, targeting a listing in late 2027. The company is reportedly eyeing a valuation of more than ₹1 trillion, with the IPO potentially worth ₹10,000 crore. The firm was formed by merging two regional entities.

stories.title: Direct tax collections reach 53.5 percent of budget
stories.summary: Net direct tax collections rose 11.8 percent to ₹14.42 trillion as of November 10, according to provisional data. While gross receipts grew 14 percent, a 25.9 percent jump in refunds moderated the net total. The figure represents 53.5 percent of the government's annual budget estimate.

stories.summary: Fairfield by Marriott Hyderabad has appointed Jogarao Pujari as executive chef. Pujari brings over 18 years of experience in hotel kitchens and large-scale catering to the role. He will oversee culinary operations, develop new menus, and mentor the kitchen team at the property.

stories.title: HR job postings rise despite global slowdown
stories.summary: Job postings for HR professionals increased 24 percent between September 2025 and September 2026, according to Bain and Company. Staffing and recruiting roles also saw a 4 percent increase. These two sectors were the only areas to report growth in job ads during a global hiring decline.

stories.title: Ayming UK acquires Northern Ireland consultancy
stories.summary: London-based Ayming UK has acquired Belfast-based Amplifi to expand its innovation and tax incentives business. The deal, which is undisclosed, will increase Ayming's UK workforce by 30 percent. The acquisition is part of a wider strategy to grow the firm's presence in the innovation funding sector.

stories.title: PwC to train 85,000 staff in critical thinking
stories.summary: PwC is launching a certification programme for 85,000 employees to improve critical thinking as AI takes over junior tasks. The training includes simulations where staff must challenge AI-generated conclusions. The firm aims to ensure employees maintain independent judgement when working alongside automated tools.
